paragraphs: We have confirmation that Apple’s original HomePod mini will miss out on a Siri AI upgrade, even as the company prepares to bring the technology to older Apple TV 4K models. The same apparently goes for the larger HomePod 2.

To be clear, Apple never said the previous versions of its smart speakers would get the new AI-enabled version of Siri. And the devices still include classic Siri and work as AirPlay speakers, just like they did before.

When Apple unveiled HomePod mini 2 during Tuesday’s “Welcome Home” product launch event, the company put much of the focus on its support for Siri AI. This allows users of the smart speaker to make more natural requests, ask follow-up questions and handle more complex tasks through conversation.
And when it emerged that Siri AI would be available on every Apple TV 4K model going back to 2021, there was hope that earlier HomePod models would also get support.
Since Tuesday’s launch event, Apple confirmed to multiple news sources, including Cnet, that HomePod mini will not get Siri AI.
Apparently, the Apple S5 processor from 2019 in the older smart speaker just isn’t up to the task. The just-announced model makes the jump to an S10.
Still, there was room for hope because the HomePod mini 2 clearly outsources some of the artificial intelligence work it’s asked to do.

As evidence, Apple’s announcement of the speaker says, “Siri AI requires the owner of the home in the Home app to have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad running the latest software version and have Siri AI turned on and set to a supported language.”
